name: Geyser Lake
full: A small spring-fed lake in the swampy forested valley of the Mena stream (Chuya basin) by the Chuysky Trakt, 5–7 km south of the village of Aktash (towards Kurai/Kosh-Agach); the entrance is through a tourist base (called “Maly Rai” / “Mena” in different sources).
near: Aktash village (5–7 km along the highway; per kp.ru ~1 km from the edge of the village to the path); Kurai village — ~25–30 km further along the highway (map estimate, not verified)
elev: not found (Aktash is ~1,400 m; the exact elevation of the lake is not confirmed)
short: A tiny (25–30 m, ~2 m deep) never-freezing lake with turquoise water, where springs on the bottom push up blue clay and draw changing concentric patterns; one of the most popular stops on the Chuysky Trakt.
desc: Geyser Lake (also called Geyzerovoye, Blue or Silver Lake) is a small body of water 25–30 m across and about 2 m deep in a swampy larch-and-cedar forest by the Chuysky Trakt south of Aktash. There are no real geysers here: underground springs well up on the bottom and periodically (from seconds to minutes according to observers, roughly every half hour according to Altapress) push out grey-blue clay and sand, forming patterns on the bottom that look like a cross-section of malachite. The water is clear and cold (about 3 °C per altai.travel, about +7 °C per awd.is), and the lake does not freeze in winter. The lake became widely known in the 2000s; a popular version links its appearance/activation to the 2003 Chuya earthquake, but this is not scientifically confirmed (amic.ru 2012: “no explanation found”). The first tourist bases nearby appeared around 2010, and the wooden path was built around 2017 (kp.ru). Access is via a paid wooden boardwalk (~200–500 m, 5–10 minutes) across the marsh from the parking area by the highway; on site there are a cafe, souvenirs, toilets and viewing platforms. Swimming is prohibited. It is now a compulsory stop on most Chuysky Trakt tours, so it is crowded here in the daytime in summer.
guide: Stand on the boardwalk and wait a couple of minutes: the springs on the bottom “switch on” unexpectedly, and the patterns of blue clay start moving right before your eyes. The turquoise is brightest in sunshine (although reviews say the colour is richer in overcast weather — check for yourself), and there are fewest people early in the morning, before the tour buses arrive. Locals also call it the Blue Lake and the Silver Lake, and a popular legend ties its birth to the 2003 earthquake. Do not touch the water or go into the lake — the silty bottom is slippery and the patterns get destroyed. Combine it with the Aktash relay station and the Kurai steppe — it makes one day along the highway.
see: Patterns on the bottom made by the springs (look from the boardwalk and the raised spots); the wooden path through the marsh and the cedar-larch forest; figurines of fairy-tale characters for children along the path (tonkosti, gorniy-altai.ru — “Baba Yaga’s hut”); grayling live in the lake (altai.travel).
skip: you expect real geysers or a big lake: it is a 30 m patch, the visit takes 15–40 minutes, and in summer daytime the boardwalk is crowded (Yandex reviews — “beautiful, but small and quick”). If you are driving past without a stop in Aktash, you lose little.
diff: Very easy: 200–500 m on a wooden boardwalk, 5–10 minutes; suitable for children and older people; on uneven sections the boardwalk is incomplete (tonkosti).
when: Year-round — the lake does not freeze; summer and September are the main season, September is recommended for smaller crowds and good light (tonkosti); in spring mud season the approach can turn soggy (kp.ru).
hours: Open 24 hours per kp.ru; in practice the entrance is controlled by the tourist base during daylight — exact ticket office hours not found.
daytime: Early morning or evening — before/after the tour groups (Altapress, awd.is); for the colour of the water, a sunny day.
how: Along the Chuysky Trakt (R256) to Aktash (~km 786–788), then another 5–7 km towards Kosh-Agach to the banner/sign at about km 796 (Lonely Planet: km 796.5; Altapress 2018: km 797), turn right onto the gravel parking area, then along the boardwalk. It is ~350 km from Gorno-Altaysk (tonkosti) — 6–7 h; ~463 km from Biysk, ~629 km from Barnaul (Altapress). By public transport: the Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach marshrutka (minibus) (09:00) with a drop-off at the turn-off or in Aktash.
needcar: Yes, as far as Aktash/the turn-off — car, bus or tour; from Aktash you can walk (5–7 km) or take a taxi.
self: Yes, fully: a sign on the highway, parking, a developed path; no guide needed.
roadtype: Paved road (Chuysky Trakt R256) up to the turn-off; gravel parking; then a wooden boardwalk across the marsh.
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → lake ~6–7 h (350–360 km; longer given the roadworks at km 455–495 in 2026); Biysk → ~7–8 h (463 km); from Aktash 5–10 min by car; the visit takes 40 min–1 h (altai.travel).
stay: Aktash has 20+ options (101hotels, 2026): Legenda guesthouse from 1,440 ₽, Garmoniya from 1,400 ₽, Lebyodka from 2,300 ₽, Nayman from 2,850 ₽, Kak Doma from 4,600 ₽ (9.6/10), Gorny Oryol mini-hotel from 6,960 ₽, Zelyony Kolobok from 5,600 ₽, Aktash Village from 6,250 ₽, Krasnye Vorota from 7,000 ₽, AL'TAIr tourist base from 13,500 ₽; the “Altai Geyser Lake” base at km 796 — from 6,542 ₽ (mirturbaz; the phone number on the site is the aggregator’s booking line). An overnight at a tourist base by the lake — from 1,000 ₽ (kp.ru 2026).
net: Aktash has mobile coverage and internet (Wi‑Fi at tourist bases — mirturbaz); specific operators at the lake are not confirmed — not found.
entry: Paid; the tourist base charges for walking on the boardwalk: 150 ₽ for adults, children under 12–14 free, cash only (Yandex Maps reviews, altai.travel); kp.ru gives 100 ₽ “for 2026”; AiF 2023 — 100 ₽; Altapress 2018 — 50 ₽. The current price is probably 150 ₽ — check on site. There is no resort fee in the Altai Republic.
transfer: Group tour from Gorno-Altaysk with Geyser Lake and Mars — 12,700 ₽ per person (Sputnik8, 2026); a private car for the day — 26,000–48,000 ₽ (Sputnik8, Tripster “Chuysky Trakt and Geyser Lake in 1 day” — 48,000 ₽). Taxi Aktash — lake: not found.
bring: Cash for the entrance; insect repellent (marsh, mosquitoes — Altapress, kp.ru); comfortable shoes; warm clothes (Aktash is ~1,400 m, evenings are cold); polarizing glasses/filter for photographing the bottom.
warn: Swimming and entering the water are prohibited (slippery clay bottom, the patterns get destroyed). The lake is in the Ulagan district — there is no border zone, no permit is needed for anyone. Chuysky Trakt 2026: roadworks at km 455–472 and 479–495 (Souzga—Barangol), delays possible. Ticks: as of 25.08.2026 the Altai Republic had 3,600 tick-bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Rospotrebnadzor) — get vaccinated/insured.
food: Cafe by the lake: shashlik at a reasonable price (tonkosti), lunch from 500 ₽ (kp.ru 2026); in Aktash — cafe M52 (awd.is) and canteens; along the highway try herbal tea, chegen/kaima and mutton (Altai cuisine) — specific dishes at the lake are not confirmed.
reviews: Yandex Maps: 5.0 (687 ratings, 370 reviews); 2GIS: 4.5 (641 ratings); the Sputnik8 tour with the lake — 4.8 (49). Pros: unusual colour and patterns, easy access, infrastructure. Cons: small, crowded in the daytime, “expectations higher than reality”, paid entrance in cash.

p.sum: A short (40–60 min) stop by the Chuysky Trakt 5–7 km south of Aktash: parking by the highway, a paid (100–150 ₽) boardwalk of 200–500 m to a 30 m turquoise lake with moving patterns on the bottom. Easy to do independently; best early in the morning.
